candidates.name: Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: National Oil Corporation (NOC) / Waha Oil Company / Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company
candidates.to: km 91 connection point in Sirte network trunkline, feeding Brega and the national gas grid

evidence.note: First phase of the Farigh-Brega natural gas pipeline commissioned; 30 km initial segment, 42-inch diameter connection to the Sirte trunkline; gas flow and pressure balancing underway.

First-phase route detail: Farigh field receiving point at Zueitina axis Field 103A to a connection point at km 91 in Sirte Oil and Gas Company's pipeline network; gas expected into the Brega coastal network by end of March 2026.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No roster row runs Farigh field to Brega/km-91. The two existing Farigh-origin rows go elsewhere: P1861 'Farigh-Intesar Gas Pipeline' (dia 24, Farigh->Intesar) and P3988 'Fargh–Sarir Gas Pipeline' (Farigh->Sarir). The existing km-91/Brega trunk segments (P1872 'Km-91.5-Brega', P1867 'Attahaddy-km-91.5', P1868 'Km-81.5-Brega') carry the Sirte-network gas onward but none originate at Farigh field — this is the newly built feeder link into that trunk, first phase 30 km of 42-inch pipe, commissioned March/April 2026. Likely a genuine new row (or a new segment/leg on an existing trunk row if the consolidator judges km-91.5-Brega should be extended rather than split).

candidates.name: Intisar A/103-Brega Gas Pipeline
aka: Intisar A/103 to Brega Gas Distribution Network
candidates.sponsor: National Oil Corporation (NOC), commissioning teams from Sirte Oil Company and Zueitina Oil Company

evidence.note: 42-inch, ~80-mile (~130 km) pipeline from Intisar A/103 field to Brega gas distribution network enters trial operation April 16, 2026, after being stalled ~16 years; recovers ~150 mmcf/d of previously flared gas.
Confirms 130 km / 42-inch line, described explicitly as reactivation/completion of long-delayed existing infrastructure stalled ~16 years, not new-build construction; trial run began April 14, 2026.
'Al-Intisar to Brega' 42-inch pipeline entered experimental operation April 23, 2026 after connection works completed; recovers flared gas at the Al-Intisar field.
Independent report of same 130 km/42-inch Intisar A/103-Brega trial run, April 14, 2026.
Corroborates the stalled-16-years framing and April 2026 trial run of the Intisar A/103 to Brega line.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Diameter (42in) and endpoints (Intesar field -> Brega/Mersa Brega) match roster P1856 'Intesar-Brega Gas Pipeline', which is already listed status=operating, dia=42, cap=42.48 — but P1856's length (333 km) does not match this pipeline's reported ~130 km/80 mi, and multiple independent 2026 sources describe THIS line as having been stalled/unbuilt for ~16 years until an April 2026 trial run, i.e. not previously operating. Two explanations are plausible: (a) this is a second, parallel/incremental line on the Intesar-Brega corridor that belongs as its own row (cf. how the roster already splits some corridors into 'Pipeline 1'/'Pipeline 2', e.g. P1858/P6714 Bu-Attifel-Intesar), or (b) P1856's existing 'operating' status is stale and this is the same physical asset only now truly coming online — a status correction rather than a new row. Flagging as a candidate rather than silently assuming (b); consolidator should reconcile against P1856 before deciding whether to add a new PID or correct the existing one.
